60: A big quality and server-optimization patch. Missing house, inn and stall crates are restored permanently, and players overcharged for spell scrolls in the first week of Early Access get the coin refunded to their bank. Cleric HP-buff and Blessing heals no longer scale with Wisdom, Ranger Recuperate is now out-of-combat only (it drops when you enter combat), Inquisitor Aura of Resistance adds 10% threat, Rogues can train Lockpicking to 10, new Beastmasters start with Revive and Call Companion, and Shadow Knight Lord of Shadows now grants HP. Common creatures drop more sellable cash loot, armor and weapon weights were rebalanced (early gear is lighter), Woodworking now caps at 300 at any level, and failed crafts return some materials. PvP /who no longer shows zone player counts. The UI adds guild member notes and rank permissions, tracking search and sort, Nearest and Front Arc tab targeting, and pink names for party members. Deep Gnome Bard is coming soon. The devs warn they may temporarily roll this patch back if the server optimizations cause problems.
59: Night Harbor is one zone again instead of East and West halves. The patch also closes more exploits involving mispriced tradeskill items and brings back missing house crates.
58: Closes some economy exploits that came from mispriced tradeskill items.
57: Fixes a housing bug at zone start that broke Night Harbor on the Trem server, and the fix covers every server.
56: Spell scrolls now cost less overall and ramp up more smoothly from level 1 to 60, and the developers are looking at refunding players who paid the old prices. Ranger snares in PvP now last 12 seconds and have diminishing returns. Cureberries are foraged by Druids and Rangers instead of summoned, some poisonous Caves of Irem creatures hit harder, a few quest rewards were rebalanced, and Underdocks gets HC, Solo and Self Found NPCs.
55: Fixes the merchant sell button, getting stuck on loading screens when zoning (especially in Night Harbor and Underdocks), and a bug when handing items to an NPC fresh out of combat. Deep Beetle Eyes sell for more, and the developers say all four starting cities now give similar income per hour, with Evershade Weald slightly ahead. Underdocks gets fishing and foraging, and the Night Harbor graveyard zone line is less lethal.
54: Ranger Recuperate is meant for downtime only: while it's active, heals are much weaker and it drops if you take damage. Necromancers get Locate Corpse at level 1, and scroll prices are cheaper for classes with few scrolls to buy. Some unintended low-level drops were removed.
53: Fixes to the chat window, hotbars and buff icons.
52: The Early Access release patch. Every class now pays the same total for its scrolls in each 5-level range, and several group buffs can be cast on players outside your group. Class changes include Enchanter charm levels and Torment, a Wizard rework with Spark of Magic, new Cleric Smiting blessings, Kick returning for Inquisitor, Paladin and Spellblade, earlier Shaman Pact of Renewal ranks, and a 60-second cooldown on Blind spells. NPC corpses above level 60 now last 28 minutes, and PvP balance was tuned so fights last longer.
51: Adds Blind Midden, with its first spawns. Brings a new character select and creation look, many new food recipes, new advanced regional armor quests, and says Night Harbor factions are easier to gain. Also has many bug fixes, including Rothold pathing, camping on lifts and boats, and tradeskill stations that only worked once per login.
48: Optimizes the server and fixes boat zoning, threat from channeled spells, Bard Levitate and pet damage. Bard abilities are now all in, and safe spots were updated for Night Harbor, Great Cavern Sea, Underdocks and Ail'Vorith.
